name: SkillCraft
description: SkillCraft is a benchmark of 126 tool-use tasks across 21 task families and 6 application domains (Entertainment & Gaming, Reference & Knowledge, Education & Society, Developer & Web, Science & Environment, Food & Lifestyle), designed to evaluate whether tool-using LLM agents can compose, cache, and reuse atomic tools as higher-level Skills. Each task scales along two dimensions: number of target items (3/4/5) and tool-call complexity per item (3/4/5), producing Easy/Medium/Hard difficulty levels.
citeAs: @misc{skillcraft2026, title={SkillCraft: Can LLM Agents Learn to Use Tools Skillfully?}, year={2026}, note={Anonymous submission under review}}
rai:dataCollection: Tasks were authored by the authors based on publicly available REST APIs (e.g., GitLab, Open-Meteo, TVMaze, TheCocktailDB, RAWG). For each task family, 5-7 tool functions wrapping distinct API endpoints were implemented. The 21 seed task families were sourced from: (i) 5 adapted from existing tool-use benchmarks (Toolathlon, WebArena, TextArena, M3Eval), (ii) 12 hand-crafted around curated public web APIs, and (iii) 4 hand-crafted around local data processing.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manually curated by the authors based on public APIs.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Tasks were systematically scaled by varying the number of target items (N = 3, 4, 5) and the tool-call complexity per item (M = 3, 4, 5), producing 6 difficulty levels (Easy: e1-e3, Medium: m1-m2, Hard: h1) totaling 126 tasks.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each task includes a partial-credit scoring rubric defining: output file existence (10 pts), JSON validity (10 pts), data completeness (30 pts), field-level accuracy (50 pts). A task is considered successful if it achieves >=90% of the maximum score.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Authors-defined evaluation harness (open-source, included in the repository).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Per-task scoring is deterministic; cross-model success rates are reported in the paper.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors will host the benchmark on a public repository post-acceptance and will accept pull requests for additional task families. Existing task definitions and evaluation criteria will not be silently modified post-release; any changes will be released as a new version with changelog.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating LLM agents' ability to compose, cache, and reuse atomic tools as higher-level Skills; comparing token-efficiency of skill-based vs. baseline tool use; studying cross-task and cross-model skill transfer; auditing failure modes of hierarchical skill composition.
rai:dataLimitations: (1) The benchmark is restricted to API-style tool use; GUI / browser-style agent interaction is out of scope. (2) Single-run, deterministic evaluation (temperature=0); robustness under stochastic decoding is not measured. (3) Closed-source provider APIs may be deprecated, silently versioned, or rate-limited over time. (4) Hierarchical Mode is evaluated only at max nesting depth = 10. (5) Per-task runtime bounded (150 turns / 60 minutes / 1M input tokens). (6) Tasks are English-only and skewed toward Western-centric public APIs; multilingual or region-specific API ecosystems are not represented. (7) Skills are code-based (Python scripts); other compositional substrates are not evaluated. See Appendix F of the paper for full discussion.
rai:dataBiases: Task selection skews toward Western-centric, English-language API ecosystems (e.g., cocktails, recipes, anime, Western movie/TV databases). Models may show better performance on tasks aligned with their training distribution; cross-cultural / multilingual generality is not measured.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: enables more rigorous, comparable evaluation of tool-using agents, encouraging more efficient and reliable agentic systems. Potential negative: better evaluation lowers iteration cost for autonomous agents capable of automating low-cost online actions at scale, which is dual-use. Mitigations: tasks use only public APIs within their advertised terms of service; no harmful behavior is rewarded by the scoring criteria; no new pretrained models or scraped private datasets are released. See Appendix G of the paper for full discussion.
rai:dataSensitiveInformation: No personally identifiable information (PII), private content, or sensitive data is included. All task content originates from public REST APIs whose terms of service permit research use.
